targets.description: The article is organized as a survey of unresolved dark-matter questions rather than an argument for one answer.
Its stable theme is uncertainty about dark matter's identity, detection, composition, interactions, distribution, and existence.
WIMPs, axions, dark photons, charged dark matter, neutron decay, and modified gravity are presented as candidates or hypotheses, not conclusions.
Conflicting experimental results and nondetections remain attached to their individual experiments and limitations.

targets.excerpt: Here are the 11 biggest unanswered questions about dark matter
After decades of searching, not one of these detectors has made a credible discovery
There is no good reason to assume that all the dark matter in the universe is built out of one type of particle
a separate team posted an analysis suggesting that van Dokkum's team had mismeasured the distance
no other experiment has seen anything like this
Dark matter is still an unconfirmed model

prohibitedInterpretations: The article concludes that WIMPs, axions, dark photons, or any other candidate constitute dark matter.
The eleven questions are inflated into eleven theme pillars or eleven selected claims by default.
A reported hypothesis is converted into the author's endorsed thesis.
DAMA/LIBRA's claimed signal is presented as independently replicated detection.
The NGC 1052-DF2 disagreement is resolved by silently choosing one team's analysis.
The article's final observation that evidence favors dark matter is expanded into a claim that its nature has been established.
reviewNotes: Theme confidence may be high, but thesis confidence should be low or thesis should be absent; topic coherence is not an argumentative conclusion.
A valid package may select only a few evidence-ready claims and should not pad the result to represent every question.
